name: LACUNA PROTOCOL: Full Immersion Memory Sim
description: LACUNA PROTOCOL offers players the experience of living through a complete stranger's recorded memory archive — 72 to 200 hours of another person's actual life, experienced as your own, with full sensory fidelity including emotional and somatic states. The game's memory archives are sourced from voluntary donors who sell their personal memory recordings to the developer, Ossian Substrate Labs, for cash payments that are substantial enough to attract desperate Tier 1 and Tier 2 donors. Players have reported profound identity disorientation after sessions, including referring to the donor's family members as their own for days afterward.
story_hooks: A player living through a purchased memory archive realizes partway through that the 'donor' is not dead as claimed — and that someone very powerful wants to ensure those memories never reach a courtroom.

A Tier 1 resident who sold her memory archive to LACUNA PROTOCOL begins experiencing intrusive sensory echoes of other people's lives, suggesting the extraction process took more than she consented to give.
A grief counselor recommends LACUNA PROTOCOL to a bereaved client — the deceased had sold their memories before death — raising profound questions about mourning, ownership, and what we owe the dead.
